evidence.claim: Pakistan says nuclear safety and security are a national responsibility and that the prime minister-chaired National Command Authority exercises control over nuclear security and other aspects.
evidence.title: Arms Control And Disarmament
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Government of Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: Pakistan says nuclear safety and security are a national responsibility and that the prime minister-chaired National Command Authority exercises control over nuclear security and other aspects.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Current government policy page describing formal structure and stated policy; self-claim, but about institutional design rather than a contested event.
evidence.period_fit: Stable institutional context for 2022 and directly relevant to Sharif's PM tenure.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct for formal authority held by the PM; actual operational control still sits inside an institutional and military hierarchy.
contrary_evidence: This is a government self-description, not independent verification of day-to-day practice.

evidence.claim: Pakistan says it consistently supported the CTBT, participated in negotiations, is an accredited CTBTO observer state, observes a unilateral moratorium on nuclear testing, and will not be the first to resume testing in South Asia.
evidence.title: Arms Control And Disarmament
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Government of Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: Pakistan says it consistently supported the CTBT, participated in negotiations, is an accredited CTBTO observer state, observes a unilateral moratorium on nuclear testing, and will not be the first to resume testing in South Asia.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Current official policy page with explicit treaty posture and testing moratorium language.
evidence.period_fit: Stable posture relevant to 2022 and to Sharif's inherited nuclear environment.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Mostly inherited state policy; it constrains but does not by itself prove Sharif personally advanced disarmament.
contrary_evidence: Pakistan is still a non-signatory, so this is policy support rather than binding treaty commitment.

evidence.claim: The NCA is Pakistan's highest decision-making authority on nuclear and missile policy, but NTI notes that in wartime or a military crisis the military would probably prevail; the chairmanship moved from the president to the prime minister in 2009.
evidence.title: National Command Authority (NCA)
evidence.excerpt: The NCA is Pakistan's highest decision-making authority on nuclear and missile policy, but NTI notes that in wartime or a military crisis the military would probably prevail; the chairmanship moved from the president to the prime minister in 2009.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent specialist source summarizing long-standing Pakistani command-and-control structure and expert caution about crisis behavior.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct for formal PM chairmanship, limited for actual crisis control.
contrary_evidence: The page is secondary analysis, not an official Pakistani statement; the 'probably prevail' point is an expert judgment.

evidence.claim: SIPRI estimated Pakistan's nuclear stockpile at 165 warheads at the start of 2022 and said the global trend points toward continued modernization and growth.
evidence.title: Global nuclear arsenals are expected to grow as states continue to modernize - New SIPRI Yearbook out now
evidence.excerpt: SIPRI estimated Pakistan's nuclear stockpile at 165 warheads at the start of 2022 and said the global trend points toward continued modernization and growth.
evidence.source_locator: table 'World nuclear forces, January 2022', Pakistan row
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Widely used technical assessment from a leading open-source nuclear-warnings institution, with explicit quantitative estimate.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Country-level inherited posture rather than Sharif-specific action.
contrary_evidence: This is an estimate, not an official Pakistani count.

evidence.claim: The UN says India, DPRK, and Pakistan have yet to sign the CTBT.
evidence.title: End Nuclear Tests Day - History
evidence.excerpt: The UN says India, DPRK, and Pakistan have yet to sign the CTBT.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct UN status summary for the treaty regime; stable and non-controversial on signature status.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State-level constraint, not a Sharif-specific act.
contrary_evidence: Not signing the CTBT does not by itself show intent to test.

evidence.claim: Pakistan said it does not consider itself bound by the TPNW's obligations and does not treat the treaty as part of customary international law.
evidence.title: Entry into Force of the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Government of Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: Pakistan said it does not consider itself bound by the TPNW's obligations and does not treat the treaty as part of customary international law.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct foreign-ministry statement of Pakistan's treaty position.
evidence.period_fit: Pre-2022 but still operative in 2022 as the standing position.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Inherited state policy; useful mainly as a constraint on 2022 arms-control options.
contrary_evidence: This is a negative treaty posture and does not by itself prove active escalation.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that analysts said Shehbaz Sharif enjoyed amicable relations with Pakistan's military, which traditionally controls foreign and defence policy, and that he would not act with complete independence because he would need to work on a collective agenda with coalition partners.
evidence.title: Sharif, frontrunner as next Pakistani PM, seen as 'can-do' administrator
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that analysts said Shehbaz Sharif enjoyed amicable relations with Pakistan's military, which traditionally controls foreign and defence policy, and that he would not act with complete independence because he would need to work on a collective agenda with coalition partners.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters-derived analysis about power structure and governing constraints, not a direct nuclear record.
evidence.period_fit: Directly relevant to the start of Sharif's 2022 tenure.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to the limits on his authority over security policy.
contrary_evidence: The source is analytical and not a formal institutional record.

evidence.claim: Sharif wrote to Narendra Modi saying Pakistan remained committed to regional peace and security and that peaceful and cooperative ties were imperative for regional progress.
evidence.title: PM Shehbaz writes letter to Modi, says peaceful Pak-India ties imperative for progress of region
evidence.excerpt: Sharif wrote to Narendra Modi saying Pakistan remained committed to regional peace and security and that peaceful and cooperative ties were imperative for regional progress.
evidence.source_locator: article summary and quoted letter excerpt
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Mainstream local reporting with a quoted letter, but still a secondary source rather than the underlying diplomatic note.
contrary_evidence: The overture did not produce a structural thaw in 2022.

evidence.claim: The declaration expressed grave concern over the 9 March 2022 missile incident, called on India to conduct a joint probe with Pakistan, and described Pakistan as an anchor of stability in South Asia committed to non-use or threat of use of force and pacific settlement of disputes.
evidence.title: Islamabad Declaration
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Government of Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: The declaration expressed grave concern over the 9 March 2022 missile incident, called on India to conduct a joint probe with Pakistan, and described Pakistan as an anchor of stability in South Asia committed to non-use or threat of use of force and pacific settlement of disputes.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official multilateral declaration hosted by MOFA with explicit text on crisis handling and restraint.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to the Sharif government's diplomatic handling of a dangerous incident, though the declaration is not sole proof of his personal command decisions.
contrary_evidence: Multilateral declaratory language can be aspirational and may overstate actual operational control.

unresolved_gaps: No independent 2022 evidence of a Sharif-chaired NCA session or any doctrine, custody, or command-and-control reform.
No direct evidence of Sharif's handling of dual-use, proliferation, cyber, biosecurity, or AI-risk policy in 2022.
The April 2022 Afghanistan strike allegation remains unresolved by an independent finding or clear attribution chain.
No formal ceasefire or settlement output with India or Afghanistan beyond public diplomacy and border-management statements.
Primary court orders or audit findings on the Ramzan Sugar Mills and Ashiana matters are still needed to separate allegations from a durable personal-nexus finding.
The appointment/favoritism question still lacks stronger evidence about whether key personnel choices reflected merit or protection of insiders.
